title: Database Abstraction and Repository Patterns
learning_outcomes: Explain what database abstraction and repository patterns contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: separating sql from application rules.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. In this lesson, focus on separating sql from application rules; then compare it with data access classes. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use database abstraction and repository patterns when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Database correctness depends on more than constructing a query. Use PDO prepared statements for values, database constraints for integrity, transactions for related changes, and bounded queries for predictable performance. For database abstraction and repository patterns, begin with separating sql from application rules. Also distinguish data access classes; repositories; mapping rows to objects. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Separating SQL from application rules
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

items.title: Data access classes
items.text: Know when to use data access classes, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

common_mistakes.why: Input can change the meaning of a query.
common_mistakes.fix: Use PDO prepared statements and bind values separately from the query text.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming application checks are enough for data integrity.
common_mistakes.why: Concurrent requests can race and bypass check-then-write assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Use unique constraints, foreign keys, transactions, and appropriate locking.

common_mistakes.why: Memory and response time can grow unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Use filtering and bounded pagination or streaming for large results.
